title: Investigation of Structural Mechanisms Underlying p53 Dysfunction Caused by 148 Missense Mutations Using AlphaFold3 and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
authors: Rustamov, Kh R; Razzokov, J I; Baev, A Y
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用AlphaFold3与分子动力学模拟系统解析p53转录因子148个错义突变对DNA结合与结构稳定性的影响，核心聚焦TF-DNA互作机制，方法先进且高度匹配本课题。
abstract: Tumor protein p53 (TP53) is a crucial regulator of genomic integrity, frequently mutated in more than half of all human cancers. These mutations predominantly target the DNA-binding domain (DBD), impairing p53's interaction with DNA and its tumor-suppressive functions. To elucidate the structural and functional consequences of p53 mutations, we investigated 148 missense variants located within its DNA-binding interface using cutting-edge computational approaches. We employed AlphaFold3 (AF3) to predict p53-DNA complex structures, integrating these predictions with molecular dynamics (MD) and force-guided pulling simulations to assess mutation-induced changes in structural stability and DNA-binding properties. Moreover, we compared the results of our study with experimental in vitro enrichment scores (RFS) and Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD). We identified a moderate negative correlation between plDDT and the pathogenicity of mutant variants, suggesting that mutations causing more significant alterations in the protein tertiary structure have a greater negative impact on cellular function. Moreover, we identified two possible structural mechanisms through which mutations can impair the p53 functionality. Specifically, some mutations, such as R248P and N239S, reduce the binding affinity of the p53-DNA complex, whereas others, such as C238Y and P278R, enhance affinity but compromise the structural stability of the complex. Furthermore, we uncovered mutations with potential rescuing effects, such as E285A and M243T, which preserved structural stability and enhanced the DNA-binding ability. Our findings provide a comprehensive framework for understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying p53 mutations and their role in cancer pathogenesis. This study highlights the value of integrative computational approaches in investigating protein-nucleic acid interactions, providing critical insights that can guide the development of therapeutic strategies targeting p53 mutations.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤蛋白p53（TP53）是基因组完整性的关键调控因子，在超过半数的人类癌症中频繁发生突变。这些突变主要靶向DNA结合域（DBD），损害p53与DNA的相互作用及其肿瘤抑制功能。为阐明p53突变的结构和功能后果，我们利用前沿计算方法研究了位于其DNA结合界面内的148个错义变异体。我们采用AlphaFold3（AF3）预测p53-DNA复合物结构，并将这些预测与分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）和力引导拉动模拟相结合，以评估突变引起的结构稳定性和DNA结合特性变化。此外，我们将研究结果与实验性体外富集分数（RFS）和联合注释依赖性缺失（CADD）进行了比较。我们识别出plDDT与突变变异体致病性之间存在中等程度的负相关，表明引起蛋白质三级结构更显著改变的突变对细胞功能具有更大的负面影响。此外，我们确定了突变可能损害p53功能的两种结构机制。具体而言，某些突变如R248P和N239S降低了p53-DNA复合物的结合亲和力，而其他突变如C238Y和P278R则增强亲和力但损害复合物的结构稳定性。进一步地，我们发现了具有潜在拯救效应的突变，如E285A和M243T，这些突变保持了结构稳定性并增强了DNA结合能力。我们的发现为理解p53突变的分子机制及其在癌症发病中的作用提供了一个全面框架。本研究强调了整合计算方法在探究蛋白质-核酸相互作用中的价值，为指导针对p53突变的治疗策略开发提供了关键见解。
